title: Night sky view over Licancabur
caption: The night sky over the Licancabur volcano, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The night sky shines above the cone of the Licancabur volcano, a landmark near San Pedro de Atacama in Chile. It is the most iconic volcano in that area, and its conical shape makes it easy to recognise even from great distances.
Licancabur stands 5920 metres high and sits where the Chile–Bolivia border reaches its southernmost stretch. Its cone makes a strong, simple foreground for the night sky.

A volcano is a mountain built up from erupted material, and a cone like Licancabur's is one of the classic shapes such mountains take. In a photograph like this, the mountain anchors the scene while the sky above it provides the detail, a reminder that northern Chile offers both striking landscapes and dark skies.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera near San Pedro de Atacama. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure gathers much more light than the eye, so the night sky appears brighter and richer in stars than it would to an observer.

alt: A cone-shaped volcano beneath a starry night sky.
